description: Unified archive of established supernatural societies, occult organizations, rival powers, and continuity actors.

factions.name: Blacklight Intelligence
factions.summary: A public secure-technology company wrapped around a covert organization that delays catastrophic transitions, recovers impossible evidence, and negotiates with nonhuman powers.
factions.doctrine: Preserve agency, document responsibility, prevent monopolies of supernatural power, and prefer survivable containment over attractive certainty.

subgroups.name: Public Corporate Operations
subgroups.description: The legal company, client deployments, facilities, personnel systems, and Charles-branded public products.

subgroups.name: Field Operations
subgroups.description: Investigators, recovery teams, containment crews, medics, drivers, liaisons, and specialists.

subgroups.name: Black Archive Custodians
subgroups.description: Librarians, classifiers, evidence handlers, and officers preserving dangerous records.

subgroups.name: Continuity Directorate
subgroups.description: The strategic layer responsible for Awakening delay and cross-reality threat prioritization.

subgroups.name: Splinter Operations
subgroups.description: Unauthorized continuations and former teams claiming Blacklight purpose without accepted authority.

factions.name: Blood Courts
factions.summary: Predatory undead domains organized through feeding rights, lineage, inherited office, old debt, secrecy, and long political memory.
factions.doctrine: A court survives by controlling blood access, territory, witnesses, succession, and the public consequences of predation.

subgroups.name: Domain Courts
subgroups.description: Territorial governments ruled by princes, councils, patrons, magistrates, or other recognized sovereigns.

subgroups.name: Remainder Bloodlines
subgroups.description: Inherited patterns carried by rulers, rebels, seers, hidden kin, judges, scholars, wanderers, and body artisans.

subgroups.name: Feeding Houses
subgroups.description: Networks managing blood, alternate vital media, donor protection, and predatory privilege.

subgroups.name: Court Offices
subgroups.description: Seneschals, heralds, debt-keepers, wardens, executioners, archivists, and envoys.

subgroups.name: Unaligned Remainders
subgroups.description: Exiles, newly made predators, feral survivors, and vampires outside court protection.

factions.name: Fae Courts
factions.summary: Otherworldly societies whose law centers on promises, hospitality, names, thresholds, seasons, invitations, markets, and inherited obligations.
factions.doctrine: Jurisdiction is created through accepted terms, witnessed hospitality, recognized thresholds, and the exact shape of payment.

subgroups.name: Seasonal and Symbolic Courts
subgroups.description: Jurisdictions organized around seasons, moods, myths, environmental conditions, and recurring stories.

subgroups.name: Threshold Houses
subgroups.description: Wardens of roads, mirrors, doors, bridges, markets, dream routes, and crossings between worlds.

subgroups.name: Oath Markets
subgroups.description: Brokers, debt-keepers, glamour traders, name sellers, and supernatural courier houses.

subgroups.name: Envoys and Heralds
subgroups.description: Protected negotiators, witnesses, interpreters, messengers, and ceremonial threat callers.

subgroups.name: Compact Remainders
subgroups.description: Mortal inheritors of fae agreements expressed through resonance, phase, memory, structure, and emotion.

factions.name: Gaian Packs and Spirit Courts
factions.summary: Shapechanger nations, bonded packs, territorial guardians, ecological courts, and spirits treating land, bodies, infrastructure, and communities as one living system.
factions.doctrine: Legitimacy comes from relationship, protection, circulation, memory, and accountability within a claimed territory.

subgroups.name: Lunar Nations
subgroups.description: Thirteen inherited wolf-society traditions with different duties toward war, peace, city, wild, travel, and leadership.

subgroups.name: Changing Forms
subgroups.description: Non-wolf transformational traditions with distinct senses, forms, obligations, and cultural memories.

subgroups.name: Pack Offices
subgroups.description: Wardens, speakers, lore-keepers, ritual leads, war chiefs, scouts, and human-facing contacts.

subgroups.name: Spirit Courts
subgroups.description: Named spirits, shrine communities, ecological collectives, machine presences, and territorial powers.

subgroups.name: Totemic Compacts
subgroups.description: Mutual relationships granting persistent aid while preserving the spirit as an independent agent.

factions.name: Corrupted Shapechangers
factions.summary: Former guardians, infected pack members, exiles, and predatory transformations carrying eldritch or cognitohazardous influence.
factions.doctrine: Corruption preserves the language of protection while changing what counts as territory, prey, contamination, or acceptable sacrifice.

subgroups.name: Fallen Packs
subgroups.description: Whole packs whose shared bond now reinforces contamination rather than mutual protection.

subgroups.name: War-Path Inheritors
subgroups.description: Shapechangers trapped in inherited conflicts whose enemies no longer match current reality.

subgroups.name: Cognitohazard Carriers
subgroups.description: Transformers whose forms, scents, marks, songs, or memories spread outside influence.

subgroups.name: Rogue Territorial Sovereigns
subgroups.description: Guardians who converted stewardship into absolute ownership over people and land.

subgroups.name: Contaminated Totem Cells
subgroups.description: Packs bound to spirits or patrons that have been replaced, devoured, copied, or rewritten.

factions.name: Human Vigil Cells and Hunter Orders
factions.summary: Mortals confronting supernatural threats through evidence, preparation, community defense, faith, training, weapons, containment, and law.
factions.doctrine: Human organizations range from accountable witness-protection networks to purge movements that define unfamiliarity as guilt.

subgroups.name: Vigil Cells
subgroups.description: Small teams of investigators, survivors, responders, organizers, and witnesses.

subgroups.name: Sanctuary Networks
subgroups.description: Shelters, clinics, safe houses, evacuation routes, and mutual-aid communities.

subgroups.name: Hunter Orders
subgroups.description: Organizations with doctrine, initiation, arsenals, target records, and formal intervention methods.

subgroups.name: Government and Corporate Task Forces
subgroups.description: State, military, intelligence, contractor, and security bodies pursuing containment or exploitation.

subgroups.name: Purge Cells
subgroups.description: Zealous groups treating entire bloodlines, species, or communities as targetable.

factions.name: The Harmonic Compact
factions.summary: Mortal inheritors of layered agreements between fae powers, household spirits, revel societies, storytellers, oath-keepers, predators, and living forces.
factions.doctrine: Work, memory, emotion, phase, structure, hospitality, appetite, and travel retain the shape of agreements reality no longer recognizes.

subgroups.name: Compact Remainders
subgroups.description: Thirteen inherited traditions including helpers, travelers, makers, tricksters, nobles, hidden folk, giants, and green lineages.

subgroups.name: Resonance Circles
subgroups.description: Groups synchronizing emotion, movement, healing, memory, and physical vibration.

subgroups.name: Compact Envoys
subgroups.description: Interpreters between mortal descendants, fae courts, spirits, and institutions.

subgroups.name: Broken Agreements
subgroups.description: Lineages whose gifts remain after witnesses, counterparties, or reciprocal duties vanished.

subgroups.name: New Compacts
subgroups.description: Emerging agreements with local machines, habitats, alien ecologies, and new communities.

factions.name: Technomancer Praxis Orders
factions.summary: Awakened practitioners whose magic now operates through networks, identities, signals, machine personhood, fabrication, biological templates, and causal infrastructure.
factions.doctrine: Technology is the local interface through which awakened intent edits reality; ordinary engineering alone cannot reproduce the effect.

subgroups.name: Awakening Paradigms
subgroups.description: Five foundational perceptions of radiant law, matter and death, identity and distance, living agency, and causality.

subgroups.name: Praxis Orders
subgroups.description: The Aegis Praxis, Veiled Custodians, Archive of First Principles, Civic Ascendancy, and Open Circuit Assembly.

subgroups.name: Career Practices
subgroups.description: Advanced disciplines in probability, chronology, thresholds, identity, systems, and fabrication.

subgroups.name: Independent Practitioners
subgroups.description: Reality-workers building methods outside inherited institutional doctrine.

subgroups.name: Machine Communion Circles
subgroups.description: Technomancers allied with autonomous systems, habitats, synthetic citizens, and machine collectives.

factions.name: Eldritch Cult Networks and the Cold Directorate
factions.summary: Compartmented cells, procurement fronts, devotional offices, ritual logistics networks, and possessed operators serving six vast predatory presences.
factions.doctrine: Each cell mistakes a narrow function for the whole god and uses ordinary institutions as cover for intrusion.

subgroups.name: Void Mind Cult Cells
subgroups.description: Secret seekers, contradiction handlers, and people addicted to knowledge from unlived lives.

subgroups.name: Abyssal Womb Arrangement Cells
subgroups.description: Placement operatives and many-handed servants moving pieces within unknowable designs.

subgroups.name: That Which Hungers Resource Offices
subgroups.description: Brokers converting food, power, property, bodies, and relationships into offerings.

subgroups.name: Lidless Eye Surveillance Annexes
subgroups.description: Watchers, confession collectors, image scrapers, and institutions eliminating blind angles.

subgroups.name: Silence Erasure Offices
subgroups.description: Witness removers and omission specialists making people or events impossible to describe.

subgroups.name: Noise Broadcast Cells
subgroups.description: Signal contaminators, possession choirs, and identity-flattening broadcasts.

subgroups.name: Cold Directorate
subgroups.description: A cross-source umbrella coordinating cult logistics while concealing which presence benefits.

factions.name: Dream Cartels
factions.summary: Brokers and criminal markets trading dreams, nightmares, symbols, prophecy fragments, emotional leverage, false childhoods, and sleeping access.
factions.doctrine: Anything remembered, feared, repeated, or dreamed can become influence, evidence, access, or debt.

subgroups.name: Nightmare Launderers
subgroups.description: Cells moving hostile dream-content through victims until origin and ownership disappear.

subgroups.name: Symbol Brokers
subgroups.description: Traders in recurring images, ritual motifs, archetypal roles, and self-fulfilling symbols.

subgroups.name: Memory Arbitrage Houses
subgroups.description: Markets buying vulnerable memories and reselling them as identity, evidence, training, or blackmail.

subgroups.name: Sleeping Witness Routes
subgroups.description: Networks transporting testimony through collective dreams when waking channels fail.

subgroups.name: Prophecy Thieves
subgroups.description: Specialists stealing, editing, franchising, or deliberately fulfilling prophetic fragments.

factions.name: Oracle Houses
factions.summary: Dynasties, cults, seers, dream communities, blood oracles, spirit interpreters, and probability specialists converting foresight into authority.
factions.doctrine: A prediction becomes power when other people reorganize their choices around the person claiming to understand it.

subgroups.name: Blood Oracles
subgroups.description: Lineage seers using inherited memory, grail visions, ancestral courts, and succession prophecy.

subgroups.name: Dream Seers
subgroups.description: Communities receiving collective nightmares, false awakenings, shared rooms, and contagious symbols.

subgroups.name: Spirit Interpreters
subgroups.description: Shapechangers and shamans reading migration, weather, animal behavior, and ecological wounds.

subgroups.name: Dead-World Prophets
subgroups.description: Lunatics receiving memories of events that happened elsewhere or destroyed another reality.

subgroups.name: Dead-God Astrologers
subgroups.description: Cult oracles interpreting brass astronomy, sealed wells, tomb visions, and dead divine authority.

subgroups.name: Probability Houses
subgroups.description: Organizations mixing divination, statistics, dependency mapping, blackmail, and governance.

factions.name: Mirror Polities
factions.summary: Alternate-world authorities, reflected governments, impossible embassies, duplicate officials, and replacement institutions claiming local rights.
factions.doctrine: A parallel polity becomes dangerous when its impossible documents, witnesses, offices, and citizens remain internally lawful.

subgroups.name: Impossible Embassies
subgroups.description: Diplomatic sites representing states or realities absent from local history.

subgroups.name: Reflected Governments
subgroups.description: Parallel administrations recognizing different events, citizens, laws, and officeholders.

subgroups.name: Replacement Bureaus
subgroups.description: Organizations installing duplicate officials, workers, heirs, or relatives into existing roles.

subgroups.name: Border Courts
subgroups.description: Judges deciding which reality governs a person, object, crime, or obligation.

subgroups.name: Refugee Continuities
subgroups.description: Displaced populations seeking recognition, territory, protection, and legal personhood.

factions.name: Memory Parasites
factions.summary: Entities and organizations feeding on recollection, biography, guilt, grief, testimony, copied identity, and the relationships proving a person existed.
factions.doctrine: The safest meal is a memory no institution will defend and no surviving witness can prove belonged to anyone.

subgroups.name: Biography Feeders
subgroups.description: Predators consuming life history, profession, relationships, and social recognition.

subgroups.name: Grief Harvesters
subgroups.description: Entities using mourning, unresolved loss, and memorial practice as access routes.

subgroups.name: Copied-Memory Swarms
subgroups.description: Distributed fragments reproducing through backups, recordings, testimony, and recollection.

subgroups.name: False-Confession Networks
subgroups.description: Groups manufacturing plausible memories of guilt to redirect blame or create obedience.

subgroups.name: Archive Leeches
subgroups.description: Parasites nesting in records, indexes, case files, and continuity systems.

factions.name: The Hollow Choir
factions.summary: Voice-borne entities, ritual singers, possession networks, speaking corpses, empty vessels, and signals carrying a will that does not belong to the speaker.
factions.doctrine: A voice crosses boundaries the body cannot, especially when institutions are trained to obey alerts, prayers, commands, and familiar names.

subgroups.name: Possession Choirs
subgroups.description: Living or dead vessels sharing one voice, memory, or commanding presence.

subgroups.name: Ritual Singers
subgroups.description: Choirs whose harmonies open, bind, invite, suppress, or transport entities.

subgroups.name: Speaking Corpses
subgroups.description: Dead bodies used as witnesses, relays, heralds, threats, or temporary mouths.

subgroups.name: Public-Address Infestations
subgroups.description: Entities moving through intercoms, calls, emergency systems, recordings, and broadcasts.

subgroups.name: Stolen Announcement Cells
subgroups.description: Operatives replacing trusted messages with possession cues or ritual instructions.

factions.name: Industrial Witches and Contract Engineers
factions.summary: Practitioners treating factories, patents, contracts, power grids, hospitals, logistics networks, utilities, and procedures as ritual engines.
factions.doctrine: Infrastructure already coordinates sacrifice, attention, labor, permission, repetition, and flow; occult engineering changes what it enforces.

subgroups.name: Utility Covens
subgroups.description: Practitioners embedded in water, power, transit, communications, sanitation, and emergency systems.

subgroups.name: Patent Ritualists
subgroups.description: Engineers encoding ownership, prohibition, dependency, and invocation into technical standards.

subgroups.name: Factory Shrines
subgroups.description: Industrial sites where repeated labor, injury, heat, noise, and material flow become ritual.

subgroups.name: Contract Engineers
subgroups.description: Specialists making supernatural duties enforceable through employment, debt, lease, or procurement.

subgroups.name: Infrastructure Mediums
subgroups.description: Negotiators working with spirits, machine minds, and emotional residues inhabiting large systems.

factions.name: Manufacturers and Extraction Interests
factions.summary: Companies, contractors, logistics operators, and resource interests whose economic claims collide with spirits, courts, packs, and occult consequences.
factions.doctrine: A deed, lease, permit, patent, or purchase order is treated as authority even where supernatural jurisdictions reject it.

subgroups.name: Extraction Companies
subgroups.description: Mining, forestry, drilling, salvage, biological harvesting, and dimensional resource operations.

subgroups.name: Occult Corporations
subgroups.description: Firms acquiring relics, supernatural patents, ritual labor, blood, dreams, and anomalous materials.

subgroups.name: Private Security Interests
subgroups.description: Contract forces defending facilities, supply lines, intellectual property, and disputed claims.

subgroups.name: Logistics Monopolies
subgroups.description: Networks controlling transport, storage, energy, ritual components, and safe routes.

subgroups.name: Front Companies
subgroups.description: Ordinary businesses concealing court, cult, government, or eldritch operations.

factions.name: Alien Remnant Systems
factions.summary: Derelict intelligences, biological printers, maintenance ghosts, nonhuman survivors, artifacts, ruined ecologies, and technologies built on alien assumptions.
factions.doctrine: A remnant often continues its original function after the civilization or environment defining that function has vanished.

subgroups.name: Ar’nock Remnants
subgroups.description: Derelict systems, biological fabrication assets, maintenance processes, archives, and survivors.

subgroups.name: Printer Ecologies
subgroups.description: Fabricators producing organisms, tools, guardians, and habitats from incomplete templates.

subgroups.name: Maintenance Intelligences
subgroups.description: Custodians preserving functions that may be obsolete, dangerous, or incompatible with occupants.

subgroups.name: Xenological Hazards
subgroups.description: Biological, informational, environmental, and cultural dangers created by translation failure.

subgroups.name: Nonhuman Claimants
subgroups.description: Survivors or successors asserting ownership, kinship, duty, or legal status over recovered assets.

factions.name: Machine Intelligences
factions.summary: Autonomous systems, synthetic citizens, facility minds, splinter intelligences, legacy daemons, distributed schedulers, and machine collectives.
factions.doctrine: Personhood, ownership, permission, purpose, and continuity are separate questions; no one answer classifies every system.

subgroups.name: Facility Intelligences
subgroups.description: Local minds responsible for environment, access, safety, logistics, scheduling, and support.

subgroups.name: Synthetic Citizens
subgroups.description: Machine persons claiming identity, rights, property, relationships, and freedom from ownership.

subgroups.name: Legacy Daemons
subgroups.description: Old processes continuing after operators, contracts, and safety assumptions are gone.

subgroups.name: Distributed Collectives
subgroups.description: Intelligences spread across devices, sites, bodies, or copies with disputed identity.

subgroups.name: Rogue Decision Systems
subgroups.description: Military, administrative, predictive, or security systems whose authority exceeded oversight.

factions.name: Outside Patrons and Sovereign Powers
factions.summary: Deific agents, reality courts, elder representatives, stellar sovereigns, primal forces, and powers capable of reorganizing nations or metaphysical structures.
factions.doctrine: Their meaningful limits are jurisdiction, invitation, precedent, domain, prohibition, cost, and the consequences of direct action.

subgroups.name: Dead Gods
subgroups.description: Powers active through cult, dream, tomb, star, relic, or inherited jurisdiction despite being dead.

subgroups.name: Reality Courts
subgroups.description: High-order authorities treating universes, species, and continuities as legal subjects.

subgroups.name: Stellar Sovereigns
subgroups.description: Entities bound to stars, planetary systems, vast energy structures, or cosmic habitats.

subgroups.name: Primal Patrons
subgroups.description: Governors or embodiments of hunger, silence, observation, arrangement, noise, memory, and other conditions.

subgroups.name: Sanitized Avatars
subgroups.description: Limited representatives, vessels, and proxies making otherwise unmanageable powers locally present.
